summary: Siskiyou County enclosed-tower lookout built in 1934 under a Long-Bell Lumber cooperative; staffed to 1956; removed by 1970; a 2012 photo shows only footings and a weather station.

facts.design: USFS R1 cabin atop a 20-foot enclosed timber tower
facts.status_note: Removed by 1970; a July 2012 photo shows concrete footings beside a modern weather station
facts.agency: US Forest Service; cooperator Long-Bell Lumber Company (register lists Shasta National Forest; location field says Klamath National Forest)

events.note: Built under a cooperative agreement with Long-Bell Lumber Company and the Forest Service to detect fires caused by rail hauling of lumber on private land; compilation shows panorama photos taken May 12, 1934
Lookout Claire Wright spotted spotlight hunters, followed them, and held two men in the tower basement until a warden came (report dated November 20, 1936)
Klamath forest chronology: 1956 was the last year the lookout was manned; register says staffed to 1956
Vandalized and removed by 1970; register gives removal year 1970
Photo dated July 19, 2012 shows one concrete footing of the former building next to a modern weather station
Registered April 22, 2020 as FFLOS US 2040, CA 146; nominated by Brad Eells

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and compilation give 1934; the 2012 peakbagging caption says the building was built around 1933. The story reports 1934 from the register and notes the caption's date.
The register's Administered by field names the Shasta National Forest, while its Location field and the compilation both say Klamath National Forest. The story reports both without choosing.

notes_for_editor: Brief's record matches the register for elevation, height (20 ft = 6.1 m), built 1934 and removed 1970; no corrections proposed. Agency is ambiguous: register administers via Shasta NF but locates in Klamath NF; the story reports both. Today's condition rests on one 2012 photo caption (footings beside a weather station) and a 1948 survey description, so the site today is not well documented. No source found says whether the public may visit; access is left unset rather than marked unknown in facts. The compilation's 1936 incident is from a 1936 California Ranger report quoted on the page, so it is secondhand. Brief's source list did not include the Wikipedia Long-Bell Lumber Company article: the cached version does not mention the lookout, so it was not cited. Worth a human check: current Klamath NF records on the site and any road or closure notices.
